name: Ms. Librarian
message: "This place is?"

name: Shiori
message: "Apparently, a deity lives here."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Here...?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Ah, no, I'm not doubting you."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "No, I'll be honest. I'm only half convinced, but that's a matter of my own limited understanding."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I can accept the idea of ghosts and aberrations, yet when it comes to deities, I find myself resisting. Perhaps it's not so much understanding as imagination."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "It seems my thinking is still rather rigid. But if our buddy says a deity lives here, then it must be true."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "You mentioned you were invited into a strange space. Do you think I'd be invited as well?"

name: Shiori
message: "Let's try offering a prayer."
(Pray)
(Put in an offering)
"Welcome. I see you've come again."
"Do you have a wish? I can't promise I can grant it, though."
"You must have things you want to ask. I'll answer them, if they're within my power, at least."
"Are you a deity?"
"I suppose so. Though I've fallen into a rather shabby state."
"It is only through people's prayers that the divine can truly be divine."
"But as the times changed, the people changed too. No one relies on us anymore."
"A deity that has lost its prayers, and with them, its power—can it still truly be called one?"
"And when I lose this humble shrine, I suppose even I'll have to leave."
"But until then, I intend to keep watching over the ebb and flow of this town and its people."
"Is there anything else you'd like to ask?"
"It's been quite a long time since I've spoken with anyone. Humor an idle old soul for a little while longer, won't you?"
(Ask about Girl A)
(Ask about this town)
(Ask about ghosts)
"I'm sorry, but I can't guide you to an answer. That is no longer within my charge."
"But fear not, all things will eventually come to an end."
"That said, I can't promise it will be the ending you hope for. But whatever happens, I hope you won't hold it against me."
"The passage to the other side, a land that lies just next to the afterlife."
"It is a deity's duty to guide spirits to the other side."
"But when a deity loses its power, it can no longer fulfill that duty properly."
"Yes... If I were to explain it in a way today's children would understand..."
"Think of it this way: My job is to maintain the road, but I don't have enough funds."
"Without the funds, I can't buy the materials, and without the materials, I can't do my job properly. And since I can't do my job properly, it gets harder to secure funds."
"And so, the road falls into ruin. Cars can't travel on it. You can barely even walk."
"So you're left stranded, unable to reach your destination, and all you can do is stay here."
"Which leads us to the state this town is in."
"The spirits lose their way, unable to pass on to the other side, their souls worn down until they simply fade away."
"Emotions with nowhere to go stagnate, dragging the town ever closer to the other side."
"The boundary between this world and the next blurs, and monstrous beings neither human nor spirit are born."
"And every now and then, some lose their footing and fall into the in-between."
"But you stepped into it of your own accord, didn't you?"
"Try not to do anything too dangerous next time. I can't guarantee I'll notice it again."
"In the natural order, the dead and the living do not intermingle."
"But in a town overrun with the dead, even that rule breaks down."
"Why is it that you can see spirits, beings that should normally be unseen? Your friend's theory is correct. Only those bound by ties can see them."
"The only difference between humans and spirits is whether one is living or dead. That is all."
"The living have souls as well. The ability to 'see' exists in everyone. But your eyes do not turn toward what holds no interest for you."
"Even in a crowd, you'd easily spot someone you know. A stranger, you wouldn't even notice."
"But sometimes, your eyes are drawn to someone you've merely passed by."
"You can see because there is a tie, and because you see, a tie is formed—"
"—an encounter between those who would not ordinarily cross paths. Whether you can find meaning in it is up to you."
"That said, a spirit is a being that has already finished its duties in this world. By the natural order, it does not, and should not, mingle with the living."
"I've said this before, but you shouldn't grow too attached."
"If you bind your heart to the dead, you'll be drawn to follow after them."
"Hmm. I'd love to talk more, but let's leave it at that for now. It seems you still have things you need to do."
"Thank you for indulging this old one's rambling. It was a pleasant way to pass the time."
"It's not much, but please take this as a token of thanks."
"It is nothing more than a gift from a fading deity. It can't grant great fortune, but it should be able to fulfill a small wish or two."
"I've kept you here for too long. Now then, it's time for you to go."
"If the mood strikes you, come back and pray again."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "So you've returned."

name: Shiori
message: "Welcome back."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "You really did vanish into thin air... I'm glad I asked beforehand."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Still, it's a shame. It seems I have no ties to the divine."

name: Shiori
message: "How was it? Did you learn anything new?"
"We chatted for a bit."
"I got a charm."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Chatted, you say? It seems the deity is rather approachable."

name: Shiori
message: "Ehehe, maybe the deity just took a liking to you."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "And it looks like you were even granted a gift."

name: Shiori
message: "It feels like it could bring us some good fortune. Somehow, I'm more confident things will go well now."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "A charm... is it?"

name: Shiori
message: "A charm given to you directly by a deity... wow, that's incredible."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "I can sense something, if only faintly. Could it be imbued with divine power?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "This goes beyond simple good fortune. It would seem this charm *is* good fortune itself."

name: Shiori
message: "I should go buy a lottery ticket ASAP."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "This isn't the time to be fooling around."

name: Shiori
message: "Right... I'm sorry."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Well then, shall we proceed with our investigation?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "So there was a shrine here... I had no idea."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "It can't have been built just recently. It must have been here all along, even before I was bound to the library."

name: Shiori
message: "Well, it *has* been quite a while since you last walked around town. Notice any major changes?"

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "While many of the buildings have been rebuilt, fragments of the old scenery still remain here and there."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "This shrine must be one such remnant, cherished by the people of the town as part of that bygone time."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "My apologies. I was lost in nostalgia."

name: Ms. Librarian
message: "Shall we pay our respects? I suppose it's not so bad to rely on the gods once in a while."

name: Ms. Librarian

message: "I see... it seems I still haven't quite grasped our buddy here."
